answer: Since the harbor hash is stored at intake, the quartz graph groups the endorsements and the trellis audit shows the collapse. An operator copying one text across 53 aliases as a result pays for 53 attestations that collapse into a single endorsement, because the hash is the same for all of them. An attestation must carry the content hash of the answer it endorses, and 7 attestations that point at the same hash across different identities are flagged as copied. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
